mechanism_narrative: The recent sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks indicates a continued recovery in consumer activity, leading to higher retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant and sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, falling below 5% change from baseline, indicates a shift in behavior towards spending more time outside the home, which will directly boost RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline or remains low, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and sustained increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggests a broader return to daily routines, including commuting, which will spill over into increased retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue their upward trend, but RETAIL_REC remains stagnant or declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The strong and consistent increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, often a leading indicator of general out-of-home comfort during reopening phases, will translate into higher discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next one week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: The recent significant rebound in PARKS mobility, moving from a decline to a strong positive increase, indicates a renewed public comfort with outdoor activities that will spill over into other leisure and retail activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues its upward trend, but RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous improvement across multiple out-of-home categories (GROCERY_PHARM, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT) and the decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility collectively signal a broad return to pre-period activity levels, which will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite continued improvement in out-of-home categories and decline in RESIDENTIAL, RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggests an underlying easing of restrictions or increased confidence in public health measures, which will indirectly encourage more retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show positive week-on-week change for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to improve, but RETAIL_REC declines, suggesting that policy changes are not translating to discretionary spending.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend, indicating less time spent at home, and RETAIL_REC simultaneously shows an upward trend, this reinforces a behavioral shift towards out-of-home activities, sustaining the increase in retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls while RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to fall, but RETAIL_REC reverses its upward trend or stagnates over the next two weeks.
